To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we quantified the phytoavailability and uptake mechanisms of AgNPs, 13 and 33nm AuNPs by wheat in hydroponics.
we quantitatively evaluated uptake of metallic Ag and Au NPs by wheat in hydroponics, and found little effect of size or core composition on uptake kinetics.
The uptake rate of silver and gold NPs by wheat is similar, regardless of the size of the particles, and the uptake is not selective for the type of the metal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the uptake of silver and/or gold nanoparticles by crop plants and how this uptake is influenced by particle characteristics, such as particle size and core composition.
the uptake of AgNPS and AuNPs by crop plants and the effect of particle size, composition, and surface coating.
the fate of metallic NPs in crop plants, and the findings will be helpful in understanding the potential risk to crop plants from NPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ag and Au NPs are non-selectively taken up by wheat.
the uptake of AgNPS and AuNPs are not size selective, but rather are particle specific.
AgNPs and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) are taken up by wheat in a nonselective manner, with no significant differences between AgNPs and the two sizes of AuNPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ag and Au NPs are taken up in a non-selective manner by plants, and that the particle uptake is a physical process.
the uptake of NPs is a nonselective process, and the uptake mechanism is independent of particle type, size and core composition.
the particle size and the core composition of metallic NPs do not affect particle uptake and translocation by plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the particle size and core composition do not affect the uptake rate constant of particles by crop plants.
the phytoavailability and subsequent toxicity of NPs is not dependent on the particle size or core composition.
the phytoavailability and internalization of AgNPs or AuNPs by wheat are not significantly affected by their sizes, core composition, or surface coating.
